children: Indian benchmark indices are likely to see a weak opening on September 9, tracking GIFT Nifty, which was trading lower at around 23,664 in early trade.
Track the latest updates on GIFT Nifty right here on Moneycontrol

Indian benchmark indices extended their losing streak for the second consecutive session on September 8, with the Nifty hitting a nearly three-month low amid selling pressure in IT, oil & gas and banking stocks.

After a weak opening, the market staged a brief pullback in the initial hours but failed to sustain gains as profit booking intensified. The Nifty touched a day’s low of 23,623.10 before recovering marginally and closing at 23,635 after the Closing Auction Session (CAS).
At close, the Sensex was down 555.23 points or 0.73 percent at 75,577.58, and the Nifty was down 144.05 points or 0.61 percent at 23,635.10.
The broader market outperformed the main indices, with Nifty midcap and smallcap indices ending marginally higher.
Here is how financial markets across the globe fared overnight:
GIFT Nifty (Slips)
GIFT Nifty was trading lower at around 23,664 in early trade, indicating a weak start for the domestic equity markets.
Asian Equities (Gain)

Asian markets were trading higher in the early trade on Wednesday, with South Korea’s Kospi climbing more than 1%, helped by gains in both of the nation’s chip giants, SK Hynix Inc. and Samsung Electronics Co.

The advance came after the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index, known as the SOX, rose 1.3% in New York. The MSCI Asia Pacific Index of shares rose 0.4%, with the information technology sector making the biggest contribution.
US Equities (Slip)

The S&P 500 ended lower on Tuesday, with Salesforce and other software makers losing ground, while hostilities in the Middle ​East lifted oil prices and investors awaited inflation data that could affect the chance of an interest rate hike.
The S&P 500 declined 0.58% to end the session at 7,673.52 points. The Nasdaq dipped 0.32% to 26,421.41 points, while ​the Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 1.18% to 52,786.07 points.
Dollar Index (Down)
The dollar index was trading marginally lower against the other major currencies in the early trade on Wednesday.
US Bond Yield (Up)
The yield on the 10-year US Treasury and 2-year US Treasury changed little, standing at 4.79% and 4.39%, respectively.
Asian Currencies (Up)

Asian currencies were mostly higher against the US dollar, with the Malaysian ringgit the only currency to weaken. The Philippines peso recorded the strongest gain at 0.188%, followed by the Japanese yen at 0.182%. The Thai baht rose 0.085%, while the South Korean won gained 0.064%. The Singapore dollar and Indonesian rupiah strengthened 0.055% and 0.045%, respectively. The Taiwan dollar and Chinese renminbi also edged higher by 0.038% and 0.028%.
Crude (Gains)

Oil prices jumped for the fourth straight session, gaining more than $1 in early trade on Wednesday after Iran launched fresh attacks on U.S. military assets in the Gulf as the war between Washington and Tehran continued to spill out across the region.
Brent crude futures rose to $99.49 a barrel. U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude was at $94.6 a barrel, up $1.60, or 1.8%.
Gold (Up)

Gold held a three-day decline, as fresh attacks on ships in the Middle East added to inflationary risks and raised prospects for a US interest-rate hike. Bullion was little changed near $4,360 an ounce, having dropped 2.6% over the last three sessions.
Fund Flow Action

Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) turned net sellers on September 8, selling equities worth Rs 123 crore, while domestic institutional investors (DIIs) remained net buyers, purchasing equities worth Rs 566 crore during the session.
